questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That the language was english and the fact that Toronto is multicultural so I experienced a lot of diversity. Beside that I knew Canadians are very friendly which was crucial since I knew know one coming.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It depended. In general the university was really not very informative towards international exchange students, most of the important information came delayed and was therefore of no use. If you very proactive you could find the information needed but it sure took a lot of time.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None. I came early which might be the reason but the info came so delayed that it was of no use. The invitation to the orientation week did not reach all students and therefore some missed it. I think that is just bad planning and unprofessional.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I am very happy I got to join the orientation, but a lot of us did not get invited or was invited so late that they could not make it. Those invitations should have been giving right away.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Three as an older student. Most of them in poor condition, so not something to be happy with. I will say I would not have done it different since there is a pretty far to downtown and it is expensive, but they should at least make sure the heat works and that the apartments are clean and without cockroaches.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: In my apartment there was a fine kitchen for cooking, but I had a friend living in an apartment with no kitchen in which they forced her to buy an expensive meal plan which only meant she could go to the fastfood chains on campus and buy the food without the tax. Ridiculous. They then claimed she could not get the money back which she had not used, 2,500 CAD. I was in shock.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: That the conditions are poor and that they should not accept an apartment without kitchen since it will be more expensive and annoying then just renting an airbnb near by.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: As mentioned above poor conditions.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Easy it was through mobility and then when they gave me the spot I had to sent an application to york and then I got accepted some months later.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We had info meetings and got mails about important dates.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted, so very easy.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't worry, just chech your mails.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was much easier than back home, also due to their curve system.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More or less the same, just a bit funny with the participation grade.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Lawyer as Negotiator, Legal Drafting, Indigenous Peoples and Canadian Law, International Commercial Arbitration

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Lawyer as Negotiator was really fun and different. Very hands on kinda and useful in practice and everyday life.

questions.answer: Doing groceries were more expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was difficult to get in touch with the track and field team at first, but after that it was easy. The athletes were not that welcoming overall which made it less successful.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: many but I participated in track and field at the varsity team.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I don't know to be honest.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: A lot! Go to Toronto Island, go to Banff, Montreal, Quebec City, Ottawa, go to New York by train or bus. Go see Icehockey, loved it! Go downtown often and to the AGO, to Kensington Market and be curios!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy I will say.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be open and ask questions to the person you sit next to in class, they might become your new best friend. And say yes to activities, don't be a stranger. Be proactive, ask them out for coffee or they favourite dinner place.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: That they are very american (thinks Denmark is a communist country) and love to small talk. Which is very little danish. Also a lot of them are religious.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The small talk and the helpful spirit. You would receive help from anyone at any time, which is very wholesome. And they speak their minds and love to give complements, which is also very sweet.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be open! Try to be brave and reach out to people, because they will help you. 
Be curious! Ask questions if you don't know, explore on your own and get an adventure on your own if no one can join you.
Be polite! You will meet people very different from yourself, so keep that in mind when meeting people, you don't always have to let them know you find them silly or different. Be respectful.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be proactive and determined if you need info. Don't take no or "I don't know" for an answer. Also the courses are easy and since you just have to pass, don't be blinded by the national students, that NEEDS an A. You don't, go have fun explore and mingle around the students and around the country.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To meet so many nice people and be able to reflect on our own system back home in Denmark.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To adapt and find a rutine. In the end it felt like home, which made it weird to just leave. Rutine takes time but once you get that it is amazing how well you can feel in a foreign country.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
